Run it with `--env staging`:

```
python scripts/export.py --env staging
```

The script reads `EXPORT_BUCKET` from the environment and defaults to `ledgerline-exports-dev` if it isn't set. Make sure it's set to the staging bucket in your shell first, because `--env staging` only changes the label in the output. The script doesn't choose a bucket from `--env`.

Before the first real run, do a check with `--dry-run`:

```
python scripts/export.py --env staging --dry-run
```

It prints `exporting staging to <bucket>`, so you can confirm the bucket is the staging one and not the prod one.

I took your word that ops repointed the bucket. The repo doesn't show where staging's `EXPORT_BUCKET` is set, so I couldn't check it.

I also flagged the stored hazard memory, which said staging pointed at prod and to always use `--dry-run`, as challenged, using your statement as the evidence. It's marked for review but not deleted. Once you've confirmed the new bucket, I can replace it with a note about the staging bucket.
